newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks end sharply off, slammed by HK dlr woes.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply off, slammed by HK dlr woes.

text.p: Concerns about a speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar rocked the territory's share prices on Tuesday with interest rate sensitive property and banking stocks suffering heavy losses as interbank rates jumped.
The Hang Seng Index posted its biggest point loss since March 11, 1996, skidding 619.62 points, or 3.85 percent, to close at 15,477.26, after tumbling to a low of 15,355.94.

"If the speculators do come and attack the currency, and interest rates are the main form of defence, that is not going to be good news for the equities market," said Robert Rountree, regional strategist at Nomura Research Institute.

While brokers remained confident that the Hong Kong dollar's peg to the U.S. dollar, Asia's strongest currency peg, would remain intact, a surge in interbank rates combined with heavy losses on Wall Street last week sparked a flurry of selling.
The Hong Kong dollar slipped to HK$7.7430 to the U.S. dollar at one point on Tuesday against an opening level of HK$7.7400, before strengthening to HK$7.7385/95 by Tuesday's close.
The overnight rate ranged from 8.00 to 10.00 percent.
"The most important thing is interbank rates, how long they are going to remain elevated," Pauline Gately, regional strategist at BZW Securities, told Reuters Financial Television.
"Institutional investors who have had fairly aggressive overweight positions in Hong Kong should probably cut those as a tactical measure and look to get back in at much lower levels."
Gately said fair value for the Hong Kong market was around 14,000 points and recommended that investors steer away from interest rate sensitive banking and property stocks.
"We have actually switched our recommendation to an underweight for the banks and we would be equally cautious on the property counters right now," she said.
HSBC, which went ex-dividend, fell HK$7.533 to HK$262.00. Hang Seng Bank fell HK$3.00 to HK$101.50.
Cheung Kong fell HK$4.75 to HK$87.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties shed HK$2.00 to HK$94.25.

Brokers said while investors would be watching Wall Street's performance tonight, the focus would remain on the currency situation. The U.S Federal Open Market Committee is due to meet later and is expected to leave interest rates unchanged.
"The U.S. conditions, tonight's FOMC meeting, really are a bit of a side show at the moment," said Gately.
Some brokers expected support for the Hang Seng Index at 15,300 points. Turnover was HK$28.72 billion compared with HK$30.72 billion on Friday. -- J.Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
